assistant_message.content: Let me check what messaging capabilities are available through the Monday.com integration.

Based on the available Monday.com integration tools, here is a summary of the messaging and communication capabilities:

## Messaging Capabilities in Monday.com

The integration does **not** support direct person-to-person messaging (like a chat or inbox message). However, there are two relevant communication tools available:

| Tool | What It Does |
|---|---|
| **`create_update`** | Posts a comment/update on a specific item or board. You can mention users, teams, or boards in the update, and reply to existing updates using a `parentId`. |
| **`create_notification`** | Sends a notification to a user via the **bell icon** in Monday.com, and optionally by email. Supports targeting updates/replies (`Post`) or items/boards (`Project`). |

### In Practice

- **To notify a team member** about something, `create_notification` is the closest equivalent to "messaging" someone — it pings them via their Monday.com notification bell and optionally via email.
- **To communicate in context** (e.g., on a task or project), `create_update` lets you post a comment on an item and `@mention` specific users or teams, which will trigger notifications for those mentioned.

### What Is Not Supported

Direct private messaging (like Monday.com's **"Inbox" or "Workdocs chat"** features) is **not available** through this integration. Those interactions would need to be performed directly in the Monday.com app.

assistant_message.content:
Yes! Monday.com does have built-in messaging and communication features. Here is an overview:

## Messaging in Monday.com

**Updates Section (Item Comments)**
Every item on a board has an "Updates" section where you and your team can post comments, reply to each other, attach files, and @mention specific people or teams. Mentioned users receive notifications automatically.

**Workdocs**
Monday.com includes a collaborative document tool where team members can write, comment, and tag each other in real time, similar to Google Docs.

**Inbox / Notifications**
The bell icon (Inbox) in the top navigation aggregates all mentions, replies, and activity directed at you across all boards, acting as a central hub for team communication.

**@Mentions**
Anywhere you can write an update or comment, you can @mention a colleague to directly notify them and draw their attention to a specific item or discussion.

**Email Notifications**
Monday.com can also send email notifications for updates, mentions, and due date reminders, so communication extends beyond the platform itself.

### What Monday.com Does NOT Have

Monday.com does **not** have a traditional real-time **direct messaging (DM) or chat** feature like Slack or Microsoft Teams. For live chat, most teams integrate Monday.com with Slack or another messaging tool.

---

Yes! ClickUp actually goes a step further than Monday.com in this regard. Here is what ClickUp offers:

## Messaging in ClickUp

**Chat View**
ClickUp has a dedicated **Chat** feature (available as a view on any Space, Folder, or List) that functions like a real-time messaging channel — similar to Slack. Team members can post messages, share files, react with emojis, and @mention others.

**Task Comments**
Like Monday.com, every task has a comment/update thread where you can discuss work in context, @mention teammates, assign comments as action items, and attach files.

**@Mentions**
You can @mention users anywhere in ClickUp — in comments, docs, or chat — to notify them directly.

**Assigned Comments**
A unique ClickUp feature: you can **assign a comment** to a specific person, turning it into an actionable to-do that they need to resolve.

**Inbox**
ClickUp's Inbox consolidates all notifications, mentions, and assigned comments in one place, so nothing gets missed.

**ClickUp Clips (Video Messages)**
ClickUp also supports short **screen recording/video messages** (called Clips) that you can share directly within tasks or chat, useful for async communication.

### Summary Comparison

| Feature | Monday.com | ClickUp |
|---|---|---|
| Task comments & @mentions | Yes | Yes |
| Real-time team chat (DM/channels) | No | Yes (Chat View) |
| Assigned comments | No | Yes |
| Video messages | No | Yes (Clips) |
| Inbox / notification hub | Yes | Yes |

So ClickUp is generally considered more of an **all-in-one** tool that can partially replace a standalone chat app like Slack, whereas Monday.com is more reliant on external integrations for real-time messaging.
